'''Clint N'Dumba Capela''' (born May 18, 1994) is a Swiss professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Known for his [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] and [[Block (basketball)|shot-blocking]] abilities, he was selected with the 25th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the Rockets. He is the highest-earning team athlete in [[Switzerland]]'s history.<ref>{{cite news|last=Berger|first=Nicola|url=https://www.nzz.ch/sport/nba-was-clint-capela-an-thabo-sefolosha-schaetzt-ld.1519685|title="Wie ein grosser Bruder": Was Clint Capela an Thabo Sefolosha schätzt – und wie die beiden in Houston einen globalen Konflikt umschiffen|work=Neue Züricher Zeitung|date=November 6, 2019|access-date=December 18, 2019|language=de}}</ref>

Capela began his professional career in 2012 with [[Élan Chalon]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], where he played for two seasons and was honored as both the [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player|Pro A Best Young Player]] and [[LNB Pro A Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]] before declaring for the [[2014 NBA draft|NBA draft]] in 2014. His breakout season came in [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17]] with the Rockets, as he saw a substantial increase in his role as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] and a key defensive player. He achieved the league's highest [[field goal percentage]] during the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]], his 62.1% career field goal accuracy is the fourth highest in NBA history, and has remained among the top players in rebounds and blocks, leading the NBA in rebounding during the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]] as a member of the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He has represented the [[Switzerland men's national basketball team|Swiss national team]].

==Early years==
Capela was born in [[Geneva, Switzerland]], to an [[Angola]]n father and [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] mother<!--in this reference, the NBA refers to players as either from the DRC or from "Congo"—in other words, from the RC-->.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 14, 2015 |others=Contributed by Calvin Watkins, Dave McMenamin, Ian Begley, Nick Friedell and The Associated Press |title=NBA players express shock, sympathy over Paris terrorist tragedy |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/14124349 |access-date=November 14, 2015 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=July 13, 2017 |title=Schröder To Play In 2017 NBA Africa Game |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/schroder-play-2017-nba-africa-game |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> His parents separated a few months after his birth, leaving his mother to raise him and his brothers by herself. As a child, at first he liked [[Association football|soccer]]. He was raised partly in foster care.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lowe |first1=Zach |author-link=Zach Lowe |date=May 5, 2021 |title='I'm thinking about dominating the paint': How Clint Capela has anchored the surging Hawks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/31388513 |access-date=May 6, 2021 |website=ESPN |publisher=Disney}}</ref> Because he was {{height|m=1.90}} as a 13-year-old, his brother suggested he switch sports. After meeting Swiss basketball icon [[Thabo Sefolosha]], Capela became more and more fascinated with basketball. At 15 years old, he was spotted at the European Junior Championships with the Swiss team and joined the [[Chalon-sur-Saône]] training center, [[INSEP]], in France.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jaquet|first=Aurélie|url=http://www.illustre.ch/magazine/clint-capela-la-conquete-de-louest|title=Clint Capela à la conquête de l'Ouest|work=illustre.ch|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2015|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170926005304/http://www.illustre.ch/magazine/clint-capela-la-conquete-de-louest|archive-date=September 26, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Élan Chalon (2012–2014)===
In 2012, Capela joined the senior [[Élan Chalon]] team of the [[LNB Pro A]].

On April 12, 2014, Capela represented the World Team at the 2014 [[Nike Hoop Summit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2014-nike-hoop-summit-world-team-recap|title=2014 Nike Hoop Summit: World Team Recap - NBADraft.net|date=April 21, 2014 }}</ref> Later that month, he declared for the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/117869/clint-capela-officially-declares-for-the-2014-nba-draft.html|title=Clint Capela officially declares for the 2014 NBA Draft|access-date=May 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140522160551/http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/117869/clint-capela-officially-declares-for-the-2014-nba-draft.html|archive-date=May 22, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In May 2014, he was named the Best Young Player and Most Improved Player of the 2013–14 LNB Pro A season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/119377/capela-falker-diot-and-dobbins-win-french-pro-awards.html|title=Capela, Falker, Diot and Dobbins win French Pro Awards|access-date=May 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924124616/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/119377/capela-falker-diot-and-dobbins-win-french-pro-awards.html|archive-date=September 24, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2014–2020)===

web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24598796/nba-draft-rockets-get-a-b-for-picking-clint-capela-at-no-25|title=2014 NBA Draft: Rockets get a B for picking Clint Capela at No. 25}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Friedman |first=Jason |date=June 30, 2014 |title=Rockets Introduce Capela and Johnson - Houston Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-introduce-capela-and-johnson |access-date=December 19, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On July 25, 2014, he signed with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web |date=July web|last=Feigen|first=Jonathan|url=http://blog.chron.com/ultimaterockets/2015/03/clint-capela-leaves-good-impression-after-performance-in-toronto/|title=Clint Capela leaves good impression after April 13, he had a season-best game for the Rockets with 10 points and five rebounds in a win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150413/HOUCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets at Hornets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231150524/http://www.nba.com/games/20150413/HOUCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 31, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his rookie season, he |url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |access-date=December 28, 2014 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref> Capela took a step forward in the postseason, when he saw minutes in place of the injured [[Donatas Motiejūnas]]. He appeared in more playoff games (17) than regular-season contests in 2014–15 and averaged 3.4 points in 7.5 minutes per postseason game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myron |first=Chuck |date=September 28, 2015 |title=Rockets To Pick Up 2016/17 Option On Clint Capela |url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/09/rockets-to-pick-up-201617-option-on-clint-capela.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150929003752/http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/09/rockets-to-pick-up-201617-option-on-clint-capela.html |archive-date=September 29, 2015 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US }}</ref>

In his second season, on November 6, 2015, Capela recorded his first career [[double-double]] with then-career highs of 13 points and 12 rebounds as a starter in a 116–110 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wagaman |first=Michael |date=November 7, 2015 |title=Rockets vs Kings |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/HOUSAC/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902233743/http://www.nba.com/games/20151106/HOUSAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=September 2, 2017 |access-date=November 7, 2015 |website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> On November 29, in an overtime win over the [[New York Knicks]], Capela recorded his third double-double over a span of four games, including a career-high 18 points.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 30, 2015 |title=Rockets vs Knicks (Boxscore) |url=https://www.nba.com/game/hou-vs-nyk-0021500252/box-score |access-date=December 19, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> During the 2016 NBA All-Star Weekend, Capela competed for the World Team in the [[Rising Stars Challenge]]. On April 13, in the Rockets' season finale, Capela recorded a career-high 17 rebounds in a 116–81 win over Sacramento.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 14, 2016 |title=Kings vs Rockets (Boxscore) |url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-hou-0021501224/box-score |access-date=December 19, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 19, 2016, Capela scored a career-high 20 points in a 111–102 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899634|title=Harden, Rockets beat Jazz, improve to 4-1 at home|work=ESPN.com|date=November 19, 2016|access-date=November 19, 2016}}</ref> On November 27, 2016, he set a new career high with 21 points against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name=br1617>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/capelca01/gamelog/2017/|title=Clint Capela 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 22, 2018}}</ref> On December 19, 2016, he was ruled out for six weeks after suffering a broken fibula.<ref>{{cite web|last=Moore|first=Matt|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/rockets-center-clint-capela-out-up-to-six-weeks-with-fractured-fibula/|title=Rockets center Clint Capela out up to six weeks with fractured fibula|work=CBSSports.com|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on January 17, 2017, against the [[Miami Heat]] after missing 15 games; he started the game against Miami but was scoreless in nine minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900044|title=Dragic scores 21 and Heat stun Rockets, 109-103|work=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=January 17, 2017}}</ref> [[File:Clint N'Dumba-Capela (30550753740).jpg|left|thumb|Capela with the [[Houston Rockets]] in 2016]]

On October 18, 2017, Capela had 22 points and matched his career high with 17 rebounds in a 105–100 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974768|title=Harden, Houston spoil another opener, win 105-100 at Kings|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}}</ref> On December 11, 2017, he had a career-high 28 points in a 130–123 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975143|title=Capela, Harden lead Rockets over Pelicans 130-123|work=ESPN.com|date=December 11, 2017|access-date=December 11, 2017}}</ref> By Christmas, Capela had accumulated 16 double-doubles in 28 games and ranked first in the NBA in field goal percentage.<ref>{{cite web|last=Feigen|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-injury-report-Clint-Capela-and-Chris-12453657.php|title=Rockets injury report: Clint Capela and Chris Paul improving|work=chron.com|date=December 24, 2017|access-date=March 22, 2018}}</ref> On February 9, 2018, he recorded 23 points and a career-high 25 rebounds in a 130–104 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]], earning his first 20-point, 20-rebound game of his career. He became the youngest Rocket to have at least 23 points and 25 rebounds in a game since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] had 30 points and 25 rebounds against the Knicks on February 14, 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975569|title=Harden, Capela lead Rockets to 130-104 win over Nuggets|work=ESPN.com|date=February 9, 2018|access-date=February 9, 2018}}</ref> Capela was runner-up for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] in 2017–18 after averaging career highs of 13.9 points, 10.8 rebounds and 1.85 blocks. He [[List of NBA annual field goal percentage leaders|led the league in field goal percentage]] (.653) and dunks (213) <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2018_shooting.html|title=2017-2018 NBA Player Stats: Shooting|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref> while ranking eighth in rebounding and second in blocks.<ref name="rockets-sign">{{cite web |last=Rish |first=K. |date=July 27, 2018 |title=Rockets Re-sign Clint Capela |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-clint-capela |access-date=July 27, 2018 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> In Game 5 of the Rockets' first-round playoff series against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Capela had 26 points and 15 rebounds in a 122–104 series-clinching win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029423|title=Capela scores 26; Rockets eliminate Wolves with 122-104 win|work=ESPN.com|date=April 25, 2018|access-date=April 26, 2018}}</ref>

After the 2017–18 season, Capela became a [[restricted free agent]]. On July 27, 2018, he signed a five-year, $90 million extension with the Rockets.<ref name="rockets-sign"/><ref>{{cite web |date=July 27, 2018 |others=Contributed by Bobby Marks |title=Sources: Rockets strike 5-year deal to bring back Clint Capela |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24212244 |access-date=July 27, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> On November 5, in a 98–94 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]], Capela had 18 points and 10 rebounds for his sixth consecutive double-double, a career best.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070822|title=Harden's late 3 helps Houston rocket past Pacers 98-94|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2018|access-date=November 5, 2018}}</ref> On December 22, he had 21 points and a season-high 23 rebounds in a 108–101 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071164|title=Harden scores 39, leads Rockets past Spurs 108-101|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2018|access-date=December ===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2025)===
[[File:NBA 2021 - Wizards vs. Hawks, Oct 29 2021 32 (51637537824).jpg|thumb|Clint Capela with the Atlanta Hawks in 2021]]
On February 5, 2020, Houston traded Capela and [[Nenê]] to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and received [[Robert Covington]] and [[Jordan Bell]] in a four-team, 12-player trade.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=February 5, 2020 |title=Rockets Complete Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-four-team-trade |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 28, 2020, Capela made his Hawks debut, putting up seven points, nine rebounds and two blocks in a 128–120 win against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/rondo-and-capela-make-their-debut-as-hawks-beat-pistons-start-out-3-0/3WHATW3UBRHOZNPP66XWDOXDKQ/|title=Rondo, Capela make debuts as Hawks beat Pistons, start 3-0|website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|last=Spencer|first=Sarah|access-date=December 29, 2020|date=December 28, 2020}}</ref> On January 22, 2021, Capela recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 13 points, 19 rebounds and a career-high 10 blocks in a 116–98 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 22, 2021 |title=Clint Capela Notches Triple-Double With 10 Blocks in Hawks Win Over T-Wolves |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/01/23/clint-capela-triple-double-blocks-hawks-beat-timberwolves |website=Sports Illustrated |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Hawks crush Timberwolves behind Clint Capela triple-double |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-min-atl/hawks-crush-timberwolves-behind-clint-capela-triple-double-idUSMTZXEH1NDB508X |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415152233/https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-min-atl/hawks-crush-timberwolves-behind-clint-capela-triple-double-idUSMTZXEH1NDB508X |archive-date=April 15, 2023 |access-date=2024-12-19 |work=Reuters |language=en-US |agency=Field Level Media |url-status=live }}</ref> During the [[2021 NBA playoffs]], Capela helped the Hawks reach the Conference Finals. On June 23, Capela scored 12 points, including the go-ahead score with 29.8 seconds left, and grabbed 19 rebounds during a 116–113 Game 1 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hawks 116-113 Bucks (Jun 23, 2021) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401337340 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> The Hawks would eventually lose the series in six games. Following the season, Capela would sign a two-year, $46 million extension through the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Atlanta Hawks, Clint Capela agree to two-year, $46 million extension, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32126511/atlanta-hawks-clint-capela-agree-two-year-46-million-extension-sources-say |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> 

On December 31, 2021, Capela grabbed a season-high 23 rebounds and scored 18 points during a 121–118 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dulik |first=Brian |date=December 31, 2021 |title=Atlanta Hawks vs Cleveland Cavaliers Dec 31, 2021 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/atl-vs-cle-0022100533 |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

On April 11, 2023, during the Hawks' [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] game against the [[Miami Heat]], Capela grabbed 21 rebounds, alongside four points and two blocks, in a 116–105 win that secured the seventh seed in the playoffs for the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=April 12, 2023 |title=HAWKS GRAB NO. 7 SEED IN EAST, HOLD OFF HEAT 116-105 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/atl-vs-mia-0052200101 |access-date=April 15, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Second stint with Rockets (2025–present)===
On July 6, 2025, Capela signed a three-year, $21.5 million contract with the [[Houston Rockets]] as part of a sign-and-trade involving seven teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-seven-team-trade-to-acquire-kevin-durant-and-clint-capela|title=Rockets Complete Seven-Team Trade to Acquire Kevin Durant and Clint Capela|publisher=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 7, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Gauruder | first=Dana | title=Clint Capela Agrees To Three-Year Contract With Rockets | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-06-30 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/06/clint-capela-agrees-to-three-year-contract-with-rockets.html | access-date=2025-12-11}}</ref>

On April 12, 2026, in his 826th career game, Capela hit his first career three-pointer as part of a 132–102 victory over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clint Capela wanted his first career 3-pointer, so Rockets drew up a play for him and it worked|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/clint-capela-wanted-first-career-170718647.html|access-date=July 4, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
In August 2013, Capela debuted for the [[Switzerland men's national basketball team|Swiss national basketball team]] at the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2015 qualification]] rounds.
